classification.difficultyReason: Combine entry revenue, per-person costs and a fixed cost, then interpret positive or negative balances.

content.prompt: The local charity is planning to run a fair, and is trying to decide how much to charge for entry. The hall where it plans to hold it will cost $\$500$ to rent for the day. It plans to charge $\$5$ per person for entry, and to give each person a show bag that costs $\$2$ to produce.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If 120 people come to the fair, how much money will the charity make?

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the charity decides instead to charge $\$8$ per person, and 120 people attend, how much will it make or lose?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Money made}&=120\times8-120\times2-500\\\text{Money made}&=960-240-500\\\text{Money made}&=220\end{align*}$$
The charity makes a profit of $\$220$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If it charges $\$5$ per child and $\$8$ per adult, and 60 children and 60 adults attend, how much will it make or lose?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Number attending}&=60+60=120\\\text{Money made}&=60\times5+60\times8-120\times2-500\\\text{Money made}&=300+480-240-500\\\text{Money made}&=40\end{align*}$$
The charity makes a profit of $\$40$.
